summary: Implement a shared booking service used by both Express APIs, backed by PostgreSQL transactions, an immutable credit ledger, immutable booking quotes, database-enforced state and overlap rules, and owner-scoped queries. The inspected routes are HQ api/src/server.js: GET/POST /api/credits, GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/event-types, GET /api/bookings, and PUT /api/bookings/:id/{assign,approve,decline,cancel}; Portal portal/api/src/server.js: GET /api/balance, GET /api/event-types, GET/POST /api/bookings, PUT /api/bookings/:id/{cancel,accept,decline-assignment,complete}. Current schema sources are api/src/schema.js and supabase/migrations/20240918000000_init.sql plus 20240921000000_portal.sql. Keep the existing routes, move their command logic into shared modules, and return stable machine-readable errors without exposing database details.
invariants: Every account, event type, booking, portal user, ledger entry, idempotency record, and booking audit event belongs to exactly one owner_user_id. All reads and writes must include that owner scope even when an id or account id is globally unique.

A booking's account_id must identify an account whose user_id equals the booking owner_user_id. Portal account access additionally requires req.user.owner_user_id and req.user.account_id to match the booking.

A booking request snapshots event_type_id, event_type_name, scheduled date/time, duration, quote_base_hours, quote_base_credits, quote_extra_hour_credits, and quoted_credits. These fields are immutable after insertion; later event-type edits or deletion never change the quote.

New bookings cannot use a missing or inactive event type. There is no zero-price fallback. quoted_credits must be NUMERIC(14,2), non-null, finite by type, and greater than zero unless an explicit future product rule permits free events.

credits_charged is null before approval, equals quoted_credits after approval, and is never recomputed from event_types. A booking charge is exactly -quoted_credits and a refund is exactly quoted_credits.
The credits table is an append-only ledger: rows cannot be updated or deleted. Corrections are new adjustment or reversal entries linked to the original entry.
An account balance is SUM(credits.amount) for the exact (owner_user_id, account_id). No other account or owner may influence it.
Approval is allowed only when the authoritative balance inside the locked transaction is at least quoted_credits. A request-time balance check is advisory UX only and cannot authorize approval.
At most one booking_charge and at most one booking_refund ledger row may exist for a booking. A refund is valid only if the corresponding charge exists.
Refunding never changes or deletes the original debit. A fully refunded booking has one debit and one equal positive refund.
All credit-mutating paths, including HQ POST /api/credits, approval, cancellation/refund, and future adjustments, lock the owning account row before calculating balance or inserting ledger entries.

All booking command transactions use the same lock order: resolve the owner-scoped booking without trusting caller-supplied ownership, lock the owning accounts row FOR UPDATE, then lock the booking row FOR UPDATE and revalidate its state.

Requested, approved, and confirmed bookings for the same owner/account cannot overlap. Approved or confirmed bookings assigned to the same ambassador also cannot overlap, including concurrent requests.
Every accepted state change creates exactly one append-only booking_events audit row in the same transaction as the booking update.
Terminal statuses declined, cancelled, and completed cannot transition to another status.
Database status constraints and a transition trigger are the final guard; route-level checks provide clearer errors but are not the sole enforcement.
Direct Supabase Data API access remains disabled for these public tables. The server-side DATABASE_URL connection is the only application writer.
state_machine: requested -> approved: HQ active owner user only through PUT /api/bookings/:id/approve. Requires an immutable positive quote, sufficient locked balance, no account overlap, an optional active ambassador owned by the same owner, one booking_charge entry, approved_at/approved_by_actor fields, and an audit event.
requested -> declined: HQ active owner user only through PUT /api/bookings/:id/decline. No ledger entry. Store decline reason in notes_admin or audit metadata and set declined_at plus actor fields.
requested -> cancelled: HQ owner or the linked store_manager through PUT /api/bookings/:id/cancel. No charge or refund. Store_staff and ambassadors are not authorized.

approved -> confirmed: only the currently assigned active brand_ambassador through Portal PUT /api/bookings/:id/accept. The booking and ambassador must share owner_user_id. Set confirmed_at and audit actor.

approved -> approved: assignment maintenance only. HQ owner may assign, clear, or replace an ambassador through PUT /api/bookings/:id/assign; the currently assigned ambassador may decline the assignment through Portal PUT /api/bookings/:id/decline-assignment, which clears ambassador_user_id. Record an action event even though status is unchanged.

confirmed -> approved: HQ owner may reassign or clear the ambassador through PUT /api/bookings/:id/assign. This explicitly revokes the previous confirmation, clears confirmed_at, and records a reassigned audit event.

approved -> cancelled and confirmed -> cancelled: HQ owner or linked store_manager through the same cancellation service. The transaction inserts exactly one booking_refund equal to the existing charge and changes status to cancelled atomically.

confirmed -> completed: only the currently assigned active brand_ambassador through Portal PUT /api/bookings/:id/complete. Do not retain the current approved -> completed shortcut; acceptance must happen first.

declined, cancelled, completed -> any status: forbidden. Repeated commands with the same idempotency key replay the original response; a different key receives INVALID_TRANSITION rather than creating another side effect.

Authorization is action-specific: HQ gate users act as owner actors; store_manager may create and cancel its account's bookings; store_staff is read-only for bookings; brand_ambassador may read only assigned bookings and may accept, decline assignment, or complete only those bookings.
database_changes: Add a new imperative Supabase migration after 20261122002427_secure_public_data_api.sql and mirror the final schema in api/src/schema.js, which the repository identifies as the fresh-database source of truth. Add new tables to MANAGED_TABLES so boot-time RLS, FORCE RLS, and Data API revokes cover them.
Enable btree_gist in the migration with CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist. Verify extension availability in the deployment environment before rollout.

Convert credits.amount, bookings.duration_hours, bookings.credits_charged, and event_types pricing columns from DOUBLE PRECISION to NUMERIC with explicit rounding. Recommended types are NUMERIC(14,2) for credits and NUMERIC(8,2) for hours.

Convert bookings.date to DATE, bookings.start_time to TIME WITHOUT TIME ZONE, and created_at/updated_at plus new audit timestamps to TIMESTAMPTZ. Continue returning ISO date and HH:MM strings from view mappers so clients do not inherit driver-specific objects.

Add bookings columns: quoted_credits NUMERIC(14,2), quote_base_hours NUMERIC(8,2), quote_base_credits NUMERIC(14,2), quote_extra_hour_credits NUMERIC(14,2), requested_by_portal_user_id TEXT, created_by_actor_type TEXT, created_by_actor_id TEXT, approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ, confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, declined_at TIMESTAMPTZ, cancelled_at TIMESTAMPTZ, completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, status_changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, and version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.

Add booking checks: status IN ('requested','approved','confirmed','declined','cancelled','completed'); duration_hours > 0 AND duration_hours <= 24; start_time IS NOT NULL for migrated and new rows; quoted_credits > 0; credits_charged IS NULL for requested/declined, credits_charged = quoted_credits for approved/confirmed/completed/cancelled bookings that were charged, and cancelled requested bookings may retain null credits_charged.
Add a stored generated time_slot INT4RANGE derived from start_time minutes and duration_hours minutes. Use '[)' bounds so an event ending exactly when another begins does not overlap.

Add exclusion constraint bookings_account_no_overlap using GiST on owner_user_id WITH =, account_id WITH =, date WITH =, time_slot WITH &&, with predicate status IN ('requested','approved','confirmed').

Add exclusion constraint bookings_ambassador_no_overlap using GiST on owner_user_id WITH =, ambassador_user_id WITH =, date WITH =, time_slot WITH &&, with predicate ambassador_user_id IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('approved','confirmed'). Map PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23P01 to BOOKING_OVERLAP.

Add indexes bookings(owner_user_id,status,date,start_time), bookings(owner_user_id,account_id,date), bookings(owner_user_id,ambassador_user_id,date) WHERE ambassador_user_id IS NOT NULL, credits(user_id,account_id,created_at,id), event_types(owner_user_id,active,name), and portal_users(owner_user_id,id,role,status). Retain user_id on credits for compatibility but treat it as owner_user_id in service code.

Extend credits with entry_type TEXT, booking_id TEXT, source_id TEXT, idempotency_key TEXT, reverses_credit_id TEXT, actor_type TEXT, actor_id TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, and metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'. entry_type is constrained to grant, adjustment, booking_charge, booking_refund, and migration.

Add credits checks amount <> 0; booking_charge requires amount < 0 and booking_id; booking_refund requires amount > 0, booking_id, and reverses_credit_id. Add unique partial indexes on (user_id,booking_id,entry_type) WHERE entry_type IN ('booking_charge','booking_refund') and on (user_id,idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL.

Add an immutable_credits trigger rejecting UPDATE and DELETE. Do not cascade-delete ledger rows when accounts, users, or bookings are removed; prefer suspending owners and soft-deactivating referenced accounts/event types.

Add an immutable_booking_quote trigger rejecting changes to owner_user_id, account_id, event_type snapshot fields, quote fields, date, start_time, duration_hours, created_by fields, or requested_by_portal_user_id. Assignment, status, notes_admin, timestamps, version, and credits_charged during the one approval transition remain mutable.

Add an enforce_booking_transition trigger allowing only the documented transitions and rejecting arbitrary status updates. Permit approved -> approved assignment actions and confirmed -> approved reassignment; reject all terminal-state exits.

Create booking_events with id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner_user_id TEXT NOT NULL, booking_id TEXT NOT NULL, from_status TEXT, to_status TEXT NOT NULL, action TEXT NOT NULL, actor_type TEXT NOT NULL, actor_id TEXT NOT NULL, request_id TEXT, metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). Add indexes (owner_user_id,booking_id,created_at) and unique (owner_user_id,request_id,action) when request_id is non-null.

Create api_idempotency with owner_user_id, actor_type, actor_id, operation, idempotency_key, request_hash, response_status, response_body JSONB, created_at, completed_at, and a primary or unique key across (owner_user_id,actor_type,actor_id,operation,idempotency_key). Add a retention index on created_at; do not automatically delete records while clients may retry.

Use database-generated gen_random_uuid()::text for new ledger, audit, and idempotency identifiers if pgcrypto is available; otherwise generate crypto.randomUUID() in Node. Remove Date.now()+Math.random() identifiers from financial paths.

Add or validate owner consistency through composite unique keys such as accounts(user_id,id), event_types(owner_user_id,id), and portal_users(owner_user_id,id). Add foreign keys only after migration validation; use RESTRICT or soft-deactivation where historical snapshots and immutable ledger rows must survive.

Continue enabling and forcing RLS and revoking anon/authenticated access for credits, bookings, booking_events, and api_idempotency. No public policies are needed because both APIs use the privileged server connection.
api_changes: Extract shared modules, for example api/src/booking-service.js, api/src/credit-ledger.js, and api/src/idempotency.js, and import them from both api/src/server.js and portal/api/src/server.js. Do not duplicate transaction logic between the two servers.

POST Portal /api/bookings requires Idempotency-Key, validates store_manager role, exact owner/account membership, active event type, strict YYYY-MM-DD and HH:MM values, positive bounded duration, and computes quoted_credits once from the locked event-type row. Insert all quote snapshots and return 201 with {booking, balance}; expose quotedCredits and retain estimatedCost as a temporary alias.

Request creation may reject an obviously insufficient current balance for UX, but this check is not a reservation. Document that credits are charged only on approval and approval may later fail if the balance changed.

PUT HQ /api/bookings/:id/approve requires Idempotency-Key. First owner-scope a lookup to obtain account_id; inside one sql.begin transaction acquire the idempotency row, SELECT the account WHERE id=$account AND user_id=$owner FOR UPDATE, then SELECT the booking WHERE id=$id AND owner_user_id=$owner FOR UPDATE. Revalidate requested state, quote, account ownership, and ambassador ownership/status.

Inside approval, calculate SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount),0)::numeric AS balance FROM credits WHERE user_id=$owner AND account_id=$account only after the account lock. If balance < quoted_credits, commit an idempotent 409 response without changing the booking. Otherwise insert the unique booking_charge using -quoted_credits, update booking to approved with credits_charged=quoted_credits and audit fields, insert booking_events, save the response in api_idempotency, and commit.

PUT /api/bookings/:id/cancel in both APIs calls the same cancellation service and requires Idempotency-Key. HQ supplies owner actor scope; Portal requires store_manager and supplies both owner_user_id and account_id. Never accept either scope from the request body.

Inside cancellation use the same account-then-booking lock order. requested changes directly to cancelled without ledger activity. approved or confirmed requires locating the unique booking_charge, inserting booking_refund with amount=-charge.amount and reverses_credit_id=charge.id using ON CONFLICT-safe uniqueness, then changing status and writing audit data in the same transaction.

Do not return success when a conditional UPDATE affected zero rows. GET the scoped resource first as needed, then return 404 for absent/out-of-scope and 409 INVALID_TRANSITION for an existing scoped booking in the wrong state.

PUT HQ /api/bookings/:id/decline, PUT HQ /api/bookings/:id/assign, and Portal accept/decline-assignment/complete must use SELECT FOR UPDATE or a single guarded UPDATE plus row-count validation, insert booking_events in the same transaction, and enforce the documented actor and owner rules.

HQ GET /api/bookings remains owner-scoped. Portal store GET /api/bookings must change from WHERE b.account_id=$account to WHERE b.owner_user_id=$owner AND b.account_id=$account. Ambassador GET must include b.owner_user_id=$owner AND b.ambassador_user_id=$actor.

Fix HQ's post-approval reload from SELECT * FROM bookings WHERE id=$id to include owner_user_id. Fix bookingAmbMap to query portal_users by owner_user_id as well as id. Include owner predicates on Portal account lookups and joins even when ids appear globally unique.

HQ POST /api/credits becomes an explicit ledger adjustment endpoint. Require Idempotency-Key, a nonzero numeric amount with at most two decimal places, and an account owned by the authenticated HQ user. Lock that account, insert entry_type='adjustment' with actor data, and return 201 with the entry and resulting balance.
Disallow client-supplied ledger ids and arbitrary zero values on new writes. Preserve existing GET /api/credits response fields while adding entryType, bookingId, actorType, actorId, and createdAt.

HQ DELETE /api/event-types/:id should become soft deactivation or return 409 EVENT_TYPE_IN_USE when bookings reference it. Existing quoted bookings must remain readable and approvable even after the event type is inactive because approval uses the snapshot.

Accept Idempotency-Key as a case-insensitive HTTP header with a practical length limit such as 1-128 printable characters. Compute request_hash from operation, route booking id, authenticated actor identity, and canonical JSON body. The same key and hash replays the stored status/body; the same key with a different hash returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

During idempotency acquisition, INSERT the in-progress record inside the action transaction. On conflict SELECT it FOR UPDATE; a concurrent caller waits, then replays the completed response. Store business-error responses that have no side effects, such as insufficient credits, before committing. Unexpected database failures roll back the idempotency row and may be safely retried.
Use a backward-compatible error body {error:'human-readable message',code:'MACHINE_CODE',details:{...}}. Existing clients can continue displaying error while new tests and clients branch on code.

Response semantics: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED; 401 unauthenticated; 403 FORBIDDEN_ACTOR; 404 BOOKING_NOT_FOUND/EVENT_TYPE_NOT_FOUND using scoped lookups; 409 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, BOOKING_OVERLAP, INVALID_TRANSITION, or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; 201 for new booking/ledger entry; 200 for successful command or replay; 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with no SQL text.

Approval success returns {booking,balance,ledgerEntryId}; cancellation returns {booking,balance,refundedCredits,ledgerEntryId}, where requested cancellation reports refundedCredits:0 and ledgerEntryId:null. Include an Idempotency-Replayed: true response header for replayed results.

Map constraint names and SQLSTATE values centrally: 23P01 exclusion violations to BOOKING_OVERLAP; 23505 ledger charge/refund uniqueness to replay or INVALID_TRANSITION after re-reading state; check violations to VALIDATION_ERROR; all unrecognized database errors to sanitized INTERNAL_ERROR.

Update both web API clients to generate one crypto.randomUUID() idempotency key per user action and reuse that key for transport retries. A second deliberate click after a completed response should generate a new key and receive the state-machine result.
data_migration: Take a database backup and run read-only preflight reports grouped by owner/account for null owners, orphan accounts, invalid dates/times, nonpositive durations, unknown statuses, duplicate booking charges/refunds, zero or non-finite amounts, and overlapping live bookings. Abort constraint validation until each category is resolved.
Add new columns and tables as nullable or without validated constraints first. Deploy code capable of reading old and new rows before enforcing NOT NULL and triggers.
Normalize legacy portal roles exactly as current api/src/schema.js already does: client -> store_manager and staff -> brand_ambassador. Do not infer store_staff privileges from the old client role.

Convert legacy credit amounts with round(amount::numeric,2). Classify existing rows linked to approvals by deterministic evidence where possible; otherwise mark entry_type='migration'. Populate created_at from date at UTC midnight when only a date exists, preserving the original date column for compatibility.
For every booking, backfill owner_user_id/account ownership from accounts only when unambiguous. Quarantine rather than guess rows whose account owner disagrees with owner_user_id.

Backfill start_time null or blank according to the legacy application's existing midnight interpretation, using 00:00, and record this choice in migration metadata. Reject malformed nonblank times for manual remediation.

Backfill duration_hours from the stored value when positive. If absent, use the matching owner-scoped event type base_hours only when that event type exists; otherwise quarantine the booking instead of silently choosing four hours.

Backfill quote snapshots from the event type and stored booking duration for requested bookings only when the owner-scoped event type exists. For already approved/confirmed/completed/cancelled charged bookings, use credits_charged as quoted_credits and reconstruct rate snapshots only as informational fields.

For declined or requested-cancelled legacy bookings with no charge, backfill the quote from the owner-scoped event type when available. If unavailable, keep them historical with a migration exception flag rather than making them approvable.

Associate legacy approval debits and refunds to bookings conservatively using owner, account, amount, date, status, and note text. If more than one candidate matches, leave entry_type='migration' and create a reconciliation report; never invent a booking_id.

For charged bookings that have no identifiable debit, insert one explicit entry_type='migration' ledger row only after reconciling whether the historical balance already reflects the charge. Do not insert a debit merely to satisfy the new schema if it would alter the balance.

For cancelled charged bookings lacking an identifiable refund, reconcile whether a positive legacy row already represents the refund. Insert a migration refund only when business records confirm the account should receive it.

Detect live account overlaps and ambassador overlaps before adding exclusion constraints. Resolve each conflict explicitly by correcting schedule data or cancelling one booking; do not let migration order choose a winner.

Backfill booking audit timestamps from created_at/updated_at where exact times are unavailable and insert one booking_events action='migration_snapshot' row describing the imported status rather than fabricating a full transition history.

After reconciliation, validate owner consistency, add unique indexes concurrently where deployment policy permits, add exclusion and check constraints as NOT VALID when supported, validate them, then set required columns NOT NULL.

Enable immutable ledger and quote triggers only after backfill is complete. Verify balances before and after conversion with per-(owner,account) SUM comparisons and require zero unexplained differences.

Retain compatibility columns account_name, license_number, note, and date as immutable display snapshots during the first release. Removing them is a separate cleanup after all consumers use typed fields.
test_matrix: P0 approval atomicity: with exact sufficient balance, approval commits one approved booking, one exact debit, one audit event, and the expected resulting balance.
P0 insufficient funds: authoritative locked balance below quoted_credits returns 409 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS and commits no booking, ledger, or transition-event change.

P0 concurrent approvals on two requested bookings for the same account whose combined cost exceeds balance: run with separate Postgres connections and a barrier; exactly one succeeds, one receives INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, and balance never becomes negative.
P0 approval replay: two concurrent requests with the same idempotency key and request hash return the same response and create exactly one debit and one audit event.
P0 approval with different idempotency keys raced against the same booking: one succeeds, the other returns INVALID_TRANSITION; exactly one debit exists.
P0 cancellation/refund: cancelling approved and confirmed bookings creates exactly one refund equal to the immutable debit and atomically changes status.
P0 concurrent HQ and Portal cancellation of the same charged booking: one transition/refund occurs; the replaying or losing request cannot double-credit the account.
P0 repeated cancellation with the same idempotency key replays the original response; a new key returns INVALID_TRANSITION and balance is unchanged.
P0 requested cancellation creates no ledger entry and is available only to the HQ owner or linked store_manager.
P0 immutable quote: change or deactivate the event type after request creation, then approve; charged amount equals quoted_credits from creation, not the current event-type price.
P0 missing event type at request creation returns EVENT_TYPE_NOT_FOUND; no booking is inserted. There is no zero-cost fallback.
P0 owner isolation: owner A cannot read, approve, assign, decline, cancel, adjust credits for, or reload owner B's booking/account even when route ids are known.
P0 Portal store isolation: users with the same account-like input but different owners cannot see or cancel each other's bookings; queries contain both owner_user_id and account_id.
P0 ledger immutability: direct UPDATE and DELETE on credits fail; an adjustment entry changes balance without mutating history.
P0 account overlap concurrency: two simultaneous overlapping POST /api/bookings calls for the same owner/account/date result in one 201 and one 409 BOOKING_OVERLAP.
P0 ambassador overlap concurrency: simultaneous approval/assignment of one ambassador to overlapping bookings results in one accepted assignment and one BOOKING_OVERLAP.
P1 boundary overlap: an event ending exactly at the next event's start is allowed; one-minute overlap is rejected; different accounts may overlap unless the same ambassador is assigned.

P1 state matrix: test every allowed transition and representative forbidden transitions, including requested->completed, declined->approved, cancelled->approved, completed->cancelled, and approved->completed.
P1 actor matrix: HQ owner actions succeed only in-owner; store_manager can create/cancel linked-account bookings; store_staff cannot create/cancel; ambassadors can act only on their own assignments.
P1 reassignment: confirmed->approved clears confirmed_at, changes ambassador safely, emits reassigned audit metadata, and enforces new ambassador overlap.
P1 ambassador decline-assignment: only the assigned ambassador may clear itself; status stays approved; no ledger change; one action audit row is written.
P1 idempotency misuse: same actor/operation/key with a different canonical body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and causes no state change.
P1 idempotent business failure: insufficient-credit response is replayed for the same key even if credits are later added; a new key re-evaluates current balance.
P1 manual adjustment: HQ POST /api/credits rejects zero, malformed, excessive-scale, foreign-account, and missing-key requests; retry creates one entry only.
P1 transaction rollback fault injection: force failure after debit insert but before booking update/audit and verify the debit, booking change, event, and idempotency record all roll back.
P1 refund rollback fault injection: force failure after refund insert but before status update and verify no refund is committed.
P1 constraint tests execute SQL directly to prove status, quote immutability, ledger immutability, unique charge/refund, and exclusion constraints protect against application bugs.
P1 API error contract: verify status, code, legacy error string, sanitized body, and no SQL/stack leakage for each documented failure.

P2 migration fixture: load representative legacy rows including null times, edited event prices, old roles, charged cancellations, and ambiguous notes; run migration and compare per-account balances before/after.
P2 query-plan smoke tests: EXPLAIN representative owner/account balance and booking-list queries and assert the intended composite indexes are usable on production-like volume.
P2 frontend retry test: simulate a network timeout after server commit; the client retries with the same key and displays one successful booking/approval/cancellation without duplicate ledger rows.
implementation_order: 1. Add failing PostgreSQL integration-test infrastructure using a disposable database and separate Postgres.js connections; preserve the current node:test style and avoid mocking transaction behavior for concurrency tests.
2. Add P0 owner-scope and current-route characterization tests before refactoring, especially Portal GET /api/bookings, HQ post-approval reload, bookingAmbMap, and HQ/Portal cancellation differences.

3. Write the additive migration for typed money, quote/audit columns, booking_events, api_idempotency, indexes, triggers, and exclusion constraints; mirror fresh-database DDL and MANAGED_TABLES in api/src/schema.js.
4. Build and test a shared owner-scoped credit-ledger module with account locking, balance calculation, immutable inserts, unique booking charge/refund helpers, and manual adjustment support.
5. Build and test the shared idempotency wrapper, canonical request hashing, concurrent wait/replay behavior, and response persistence.
6. Build and test the shared booking command service with the fixed lock order, transition authorization, audit writes, database-error mapping, and no event-price recomputation during approval.
7. Replace Portal POST /api/bookings with quote snapshot creation and database overlap enforcement; update Portal reads to include owner scope.
8. Replace HQ approval, decline, assign, and cancellation handlers with the shared service; then replace Portal cancel, accept, decline-assignment, and complete handlers.
9. Harden HQ POST /api/credits, event-type deletion/deactivation, all post-command reloads, and portal-user/account joins.
10. Update response mappers and both web clients for quotedCredits, stable error codes, actor-appropriate buttons, and idempotency-key generation/reuse.
11. Run the legacy-data preflight and reconciliation in a production copy or staging database, verify exact per-account balance parity, then validate constraints and enable immutable triggers.
12. Run both API test suites plus the P0/P1 database integration matrix, perform concurrent stress repetitions, and only then deploy the migration before the application release.
risks: The checkout has staged security work and modified schema/migration files. Implementation must preserve those changes and avoid treating the clean origin/main revision as the complete target.
api/src/schema.js creates tables at runtime while Supabase migrations also define them. Updating only one path will produce divergent fresh and upgraded databases.
Legacy DOUBLE PRECISION values may not convert exactly to two-decimal NUMERIC. Migration must report every rounded value and prove per-account balance parity.
Existing data may contain malformed text dates/times, missing event types, zero-cost bookings, owner mismatches, or overlaps that prevent constraint validation.

The btree_gist extension must be available and permitted. If it is not, the fallback is transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock keys for owner/account/date and owner/ambassador/date plus overlap queries, but that is weaker than declarative exclusion constraints and every writer must use it.

Changing Portal cancellation authorization from all non-ambassadors to store_manager only may expose a product expectation for store_staff. The role decision should be confirmed before release, but the database transaction remains shared either way.

Making Idempotency-Key mandatory requires coordinated web-client deployment. A compatibility window may accept a server-generated key only for nonfinancial commands, but financial commands should not silently lose retry safety.
Soft-deactivating event types and retaining accounts with financial history changes current delete behavior. UI copy and API errors must explain why historical records cannot be physically removed.

Long-lived account-row locks serialize financial actions for one account by design. Keep transactions small, perform no network calls inside them, and set a bounded lock_timeout with a retryable 409 or 503 mapping.
Exclusion constraints can surface 23P01 after a route-level precheck because another transaction won the race. Error mapping must use SQLSTATE/constraint names rather than message text.

Idempotency records containing response bodies may grow indefinitely. Define an operational retention policy only after establishing the maximum client retry horizon and preserving financial request keys.

The current UI derives some completed display states from past dates without updating the database. Database status remains authoritative; automatic completion should not be introduced implicitly by this ledger change.
No live Supabase service was contacted for this read-only specification. Extension availability, migration execution time, and real legacy-data quality remain deployment checks.
